title: Independent remediation validation and release gates
description: Define layered release gates for remediation outputs: independent machine validation, semantic correctness review by a human, and assistive-technology review. Include failure classification and traceable audit evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: define failing validator-fixture tests, false-positive/false-negative handling, accessibility tree checks, and human review checklist cases before wiring gates. Include veraPDF as a candidate machine-only validator, not proof of WCAG conformance. DoD: machine checks do not replace human semantic or assistive-technology gates; tagged output alone is never called PDF/UA or WCAG compliant.

title: Build synthetic characterization and gold fixture plan
description: Define a versioned synthetic/deidentified fixture corpus and characterization strategy for existing PDFs across statements, invoices, correspondence, and reports. Capture expected input behavior and preservation constraints before remediation changes.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: author fixture manifests and failing characterization assertions before any writer or repair code. Cover visible text, layout, page count, reading order where known, links/forms/annotations where applicable, language and metadata. Include malformed, scanned, and mixed-content cases only as synthetic fixtures. DoD: fixture provenance and safe handling are documented; never migrate prior private reports or sample documents.

title: Define document data, accessibility, and security profiles
description: Inventory the profile decisions that affect processing and acceptance: statements, invoices, correspondence, and reports; source data fields; language; confidentiality; retention; accessibility expectations; and human review needs. Use synthetic/deidentified examples only. Keep unresolved choices explicitly proposed.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: define profile schema examples and invalid/ambiguous cases, then assert validation behavior in contract tests. Include representative examples for all four document families. Red/green/refactor the schema and docs; record decisions and unresolved owner questions. DoD: no real sample documents or private reports; fixture and threat-data handling rules are documented.

title: Existing-PDF writer and fidelity feasibility spike
description:
Probe whether an open-source PDF writer can preserve the required existing-PDF structures and visible fidelity while adding/remapping accessibility structure. Evaluate Apache-2.0 PDFBox as a candidate alongside alternatives. Scope this as a Go adapter feasibility question, not a Go PDF library assumption. Use synthetic/deidentified gold fixtures covering the four families.

## Goal

Run a bounded, test-first feasibility investigation using synthetic or safely sourced non-confidential fixtures.

## Findings

Pending the spike. Record reproducible observations, exact versions and licenses, limitations, and an evidence-backed recommendation before closing this issue.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: before implementation, define characterization snapshots and preservation assertions for visible text, page geometry/rendering, links, forms, annotations, fonts, and metadata as applicable. Run a minimal writer round-trip spike, measure fixture diffs only (no invented target), document failure modes, licensing, and a go/no-go decision. No production writer is selected until this gate passes.

title: Cross-lane failure, security, and end-to-end gates
description: Define shared failure-injection, security, privacy, and end-to-end gates spanning generation and remediation while keeping their pipelines separately testable.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: specify adversarial synthetic inputs, malformed PDFs, hostile metadata, resource exhaustion, worker timeout/crash, retry/idempotence, data-leakage, and audit-integrity tests. Add layered unit/contract/integration/end-to-end checks and verify test fixtures contain no private data. DoD: negative paths are observable and fail safely; lane-specific results and human gates remain distinguishable.

title: Vertical slices: statements and invoices
description: Plan test-driven generation slices for statement and invoice documents from validated synthetic data and templates through the selected PDF engine.
acceptance_criteria: For each family, write failing golden tests first for totals/data integrity, reading order, headings, table headers, links, language, visible layout, and generated structure. Implement one vertical slice at a time, refactor with the test suite green, then run independent machine and human semantic/assistive-technology checks. DoD: data-to-PDF traceability; no compliance claim without all gates.

title: Vertical slices: correspondence and reports
description: Plan test-driven generation slices for correspondence and report documents from validated synthetic data and templates through the selected PDF engine.
acceptance_criteria: For each family, write failing golden tests first for hierarchy, paragraphs, lists, figures/tables, links, language, visible layout, and generated structure. Implement one vertical slice at a time, refactor with tests green, then run independent machine and human semantic/assistive-technology checks. DoD: ambiguity routes to review; no compliance claim without all gates.

title: Test-first data and template model
description: Define a validated input model and template boundary for statements, invoices, correspondence, and reports, including provenance, localization, semantic roles, and accessibility metadata. Use generated synthetic data only.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: define fixture tables for each family, missing/invalid/unsafe fields, escaping, localization, and semantic template requirements. Implement model/template validation and refactor only with unit tests green. DoD: data decisions and privacy handling are explicit and unresolved choices remain proposed.

title: DOCX and Markdown source workflow feasibility
description:
Evaluate how DOCX and Markdown inputs or authored source documents fit the generation lane, including preservation of semantics through conversion to the selected PDF engine. Distinguish generation from existing-PDF remediation.

## Goal

Run a bounded, test-first feasibility investigation using synthetic or safely sourced non-confidential fixtures.

## Findings

Pending the spike. Record reproducible observations, exact versions and licenses, limitations, and an evidence-backed recommendation before closing this issue.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: create paired synthetic DOCX/Markdown inputs and expected semantic/layout properties before conversion trials. Compare extracted text, headings, lists, tables, links, language, and metadata. Record tested tool/license constraints and gaps; do not select a converter without evidence.

title: Vertical slice: semantic and complex-content repair
description: Extend remediation after the baseline slice to selected heading/reading order, figures/alt text, tables, lists, language, and document metadata cases where inputs support reliable repair; preserve original meaning and visible fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: add failing gold-fixture, unit, adapter-contract, and preservation tests for each selected semantic case. Implement, then refactor under green tests. Include ambiguous content as a human-review route, not a guessed repair. DoD: all four document families remain represented; unsupported cases are explicit.

title: Specify remediation worker adapter contracts
description: Define stable Go interfaces around the remediation orchestration and replaceable open-source worker adapters: inspect, classify, propose semantic repair, write, validate, and report audit evidence. Keep vendor/tool details behind adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: write contract tests for valid/invalid inputs, deterministic output/evidence shape, timeouts, cancellation, idempotence expectations, unsupported features, tool failures, and license policy. Start with failing tests, implement the smallest contract, then refactor. DoD: no product code dependency on enterprise-only tagging/export.

title: Vertical slice: baseline structure repair
description: Plan a first narrow existing-PDF remediation slice against synthetic fixtures after the writer/fidelity gate: preserve visible content while adding a minimal, auditable structure repair for one selected representative family.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: add failing unit tests for semantic repair decisions, worker contract tests, and preservation assertions; implement only enough adapter/writer behavior to pass; refactor with tests green. Integrate an independent validator and human review record. DoD: evidence identifies what was machine-checked and what requires human review; no compliance claim follows from tags alone.

title: Verify open-source remediation tools and license boundaries
description:
Verify current licenses, versions, capabilities, maintenance, and integration boundaries for candidate remediation tools: OpenDataLoader OSS auto-tagging (exclude enterprise-only PDF/UA export), PDFBox custom writer, veraPDF machine validation, qpdf structural operations, and selective OCRmyPDF/Tesseract. Treat every item as a candidate, not an accepted dependency.

## Goal

Run a bounded, test-first feasibility investigation using synthetic or safely sourced non-confidential fixtures.

## Findings

Pending the spike. Record reproducible observations, exact versions and licenses, limitations, and an evidence-backed recommendation before closing this issue.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: define adapter capability and license-policy contract cases, including rejection of an enterprise-only dependency and verification of license metadata. Exercise representative synthetic fixtures with available candidates. Record exact verified versions, licenses, limitations, and unresolved compatibility questions. DoD: no commercial-only component is an accepted remediation dependency.

title: Record cross-lane architecture and acceptance decisions
description:
Use spike evidence to record proposed architecture decisions for the Go API/job orchestration/audit/semantic repair control plane, replaceable remediation worker adapters, and independent generation lane. Make data profiles, PDF writer/fidelity, generation engine, and compliance target explicit decision points.

## Rationale

This decision remains open until the linked profile and feasibility work provides reviewable evidence.

## Alternatives Considered

Compare viable options and record evidence, tradeoffs, and consequences before approval. No option is selected yet.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: create a decision checklist and validate that every gate has evidence, test fixtures, acceptance owner, alternatives, and status. Red/green/refactor the decision record format as needed. DoD: accepted vs proposed is explicit; no unverified engine, compliance level, or production design is presented as approved.

title: Generation PDF engine selection spike
description:
Evaluate generation engines for the generation lane without presuming PDFBox or another engine is selected. Consider the Go-centered control plane, replaceable adapters, data/template integration, accessible output support, output fidelity, licensing, operations, and testability.

## Goal

Run a bounded, test-first feasibility investigation using synthetic or safely sourced non-confidential fixtures.

## Findings

Pending the spike. Record reproducible observations, exact versions and licenses, limitations, and an evidence-backed recommendation before closing this issue.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: define synthetic generation golden cases for statements, invoices, correspondence, and reports, plus source-to-output text/layout and structure checks. Prototype only the smallest comparative spike needed. Record verified capability/license evidence, tradeoffs, and a proposed selection gate; no engine choice until evidence passes.

title: Milestone: IBM AFP migration feasibility
description: Evaluate IBM AFP print-stream migration as a distinct feasibility track, separate from the accessible PDF lanes.
acceptance_criteria: A bounded test-first feasibility report identifies representative synthetic inputs, conversion options, preservation checks, licensing, operational constraints, and a go/no-go recommendation without presuming migration.

title: Milestone: open-source PDF remediation
description: Plan the open-source existing-PDF accessibility remediation path using a Go-centered control plane and replaceable worker adapters.
acceptance_criteria: All remediation dependencies are open-source-only and verified; synthetic gold fixtures, preservation behavior, machine validation, human semantic review, and assistive-technology checks gate release.

title: Milestone: accessible document generation
description: Plan the generation lane from data/templates and source formats through a selected PDF engine, keeping engine selection explicitly unresolved until a spike passes.
acceptance_criteria: Statements, invoices, correspondence, and reports have test-first acceptance slices; DOCX and Markdown are in scope; generated tagging is independently validated and never treated as compliance by itself.

title: Milestone: profiles and feasibility gates
description: Resolve data/profile requirements and feasibility questions before committing to production designs across the two product lanes.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence-backed decisions and open questions are recorded; required feasibility spikes have reproducible tests and no production architecture is presumed.

title: Roadmap: test-driven product delivery
description: Umbrella epic for the staged accessible document pipeline roadmap. Covers both open-source existing-PDF remediation and accessible document generation, with shared data/profile governance and a distinct IBM AFP feasibility track. Planning only: no production implementation, approved architecture, schedule, budget, performance target, or compliance claim is established by this epic.
acceptance_criteria: Each milestone has an ordered dependency graph, test-first acceptance criteria, evidence gates, and no invented timeline or measured result. Remediation dependencies remain open-source-only; no enterprise-only tagging/export dependency is accepted. All four families (statements, invoices, correspondence, reports) are explicitly represented in test fixture planning. Tagged output is not stated as PDF/UA or WCAG compliant without independent machine and human gates.

title: AFP migration feasibility experiment
description:
Evaluate IBM AFP print migration as a separate feasibility question. Do not assume the desired input/output workflow or whether AFP must be converted to PDF or remain printable; record those questions.

## Goal

Run a bounded, test-first feasibility investigation using synthetic or safely sourced non-confidential fixtures.

## Findings

Pending the spike. Record reproducible observations, exact versions and licenses, limitations, and an evidence-backed recommendation before closing this issue.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: define synthetic AFP-like input expectations or a safely sourced non-confidential fixture plan and preservation checks before evaluating conversion. Assess representative layouts, fonts, barcodes, pagination, variable data, licensing, and operations. Deliver evidence-backed go/no-go options and unresolved questions; do not implement migration.
